title: General writing template
intro: A short summary of each section's structure and basic rules, in the order the paper prints them. Each section's contract in sections/ holds the full rule set and its disqualifiers; this panel only condenses it.

sections.name: Title and keywords

structure.label: Title slots
structure.text: Optional acronym with a colon, optional article, then the required property adjective (first), the required mechanism, an optional artefact noun, the required task, and a domain or place only when the work is bound to it.

structure.label: Source of the slots
structure.text: Property, mechanism and task come from the proposal: the property the contributions add, the mechanism that realizes them, the task the problem statement named.

structure.label: Keywords
structure.text: Three to five, separated by semicolons, ordered broadest to most specific: task or domain, then property, then machinery.

structure.label: Author header
structure.text: Blinded placeholder while drafting; when the operator reveals the authors, the author header uses the wrapping minipage template (no overflow).

rules: No number, no percentage, no comparative, no claim of superiority.
Title case, prepositions and articles in lower case; a hyphen joins a modifier pair, an en dash joins co-equal terms.
An acronym in the title takes a colon and the abstract expands it.

Keywords are not a restatement of the title: about a third repeat a title term, the rest add omitted mechanisms, the data modality or population, and the property in its noun form; every keyword appears in the body.
The manuscript is typeset in single-column review mode (onecolumn); no real author names, affiliations or e-mails until the whole manuscript is verified with the operator.

sections.name: Abstract

structure.label: Slot 1 — Context
structure.text: 1–2 sentences: the field and the phenomenon the dataset contains, and why failure there is costly.

structure.label: Slot 2 — Problem
structure.text: 1–2 sentences opening with an adversative; names the specific shortcoming, the state of the art absorbed as half a clause.

structure.label: Slot 3 — The proposal, named
structure.text: Exactly one sentence: full name, acronym, artefact category and the one new mechanism.

structure.label: Slot 4 — Announcement and components
structure.text: The count of contributions announced, then enumerated inline (one sentence of 49–85 words) or expanded (one sentence each); never mixed. The longest slot.

structure.label: Slot 5 — Validation
structure.text: 1–4 sentences: scenario, data or tasks, compared methods, criteria or metrics, complementary analyses, in that order.

structure.label: Slot 6 — Result or secondary contribution
structure.text: 1–2 sentences; a figure only when it is the fact being framed, stating what it belongs to and matching the results exactly.

structure.label: Slot 7 — Verdict
structure.text: Exactly one sentence, the last one, 11–28 words; introduces nothing new.

rules: No citation, equation, figure, table or section reference.
No unexpanded acronym and no forward reference: the abstract is self-contained.
No named family of prior methods and no walked lineage; the organization of the article never appears.
Component count, order and naming agree with the introduction and the methods section.
Every property claimed has its instrument named in slot 5.

sections.name: Introduction

structure.label: Paragraph 1 — Application context
structure.text: 145–200 words: the application domain and the motivating phenomenon the dataset contains, never the family of methods; no dataset named.

structure.label: Paragraph 2 — AI context and problem
structure.text: 130–220 words: AI techniques in that application, closing with two or three sentences declaring the technical problem and its root causes; running text, no bullets, no bold, no numbered questions.

structure.label: Paragraph 3 — State of the art, first families
structure.text: 130–300 words: the first methodological families with their primary methods, strengths and limitations; each paragraph ends on a limitation.

structure.label: Paragraph 4 — Remaining families and joint gap
structure.text: 130–300 words: the remaining families in the same form, closing on the joint gap; paragraphs 3 and 4 present 3 to 7 families.

structure.label: Paragraph 5 — Proposal and contributions
structure.text: 120–180 words: the proposal presentation ending in a colon, followed by 3 to 4 short contribution items that continue the paragraph.

structure.label: Paragraph 6 — Evaluation, results and impact
structure.text: 65–135 words: experiments, comparison methods, evaluation criteria and potential impact; no figure, percentage or value.

structure.label: Paragraph 7 — Roadmap
structure.text: 32–42 words: the organization of the paper in a fixed roadmap formula, naming only sections that exist.

rules: No equations, figures or tables.
The chain problem → limitation → contribution → property → instrument → evidence keeps the same name for each property through every link, never a synonym.
Citations close the sentence they support, never as a noun phrase, and appear only up to block 3, besides 4a's citation of the prior work the proposal extends.
Contribution items never open in bold or as a description label; their count, order and naming match the methods section.
No panorama paragraph and, when a Related Work section exists, no variants or alternative strategies in block 3.

sections.name: Related work
sections.extent: 820–1700 words · paragraphs of 130–300 words · one synthesis table of 7–12 works

structure.label: Block 1 — Preamble
structure.text: One paragraph of about 40 words, two sentences, no citations, naming the blocks that follow.

structure.label: Block 2 — General panorama
structure.text: One paragraph of about 150 words: the trajectory of the general problem, without developing any family.

structure.label: Block 3 — One block per specific problem or family
structure.text: One subsection per family of the introduction, 2 to 3 paragraphs each (foundations, main methods, main challenges), each paragraph closing on its family's limitation; 5 to 10 distinct works cited per family.

structure.label: Block 4 — Open fronts and the gap
structure.text: One paragraph of 100–125 words, 3 to 5 sentences: recapitulation, the open fronts (one per block), and which the proposal attacks, closing on its name.

structure.label: Block 5 — Synthesis artefact
structure.text: A comparison table of 7 to 12 works whose dimensions are the properties the proposal wins on, introduced by a one-sentence pointer that names them; the proposal is the last row.

rules: The section exists only when a problem's lineage needs more than one paragraph or the comparison table is wanted.
Thematic, not catalogue: sentences are about families, never a citation used as a noun phrase.
Two to six citations per paragraph, each at the end of the sentence it supports; every limitation of prior work is cited.
No equations; no paragraph longer than 300 words.
Introduction and related work together cite 30 to 40 references.

sections.name: Materials and methods
sections.extent: 1000–3950 words · 2 to 9 subsections · one summary diagram

structure.label: Preamble (optional)
structure.text: One paragraph of 60–120 words, no citations, naming the method once and the subsections in order.

structure.label: Slot 1 — The dataset (when this section owns it)
structure.text: 3–12 paragraphs: why these data and their provenance, one paragraph per dataset, acquisition protocol, what was discarded then the preprocessing kept, how a sample is built, how subjects stay together across splits. When a real dataset is described, its explanation closes with an acquisition-protocol diagram drawn by the diagram-author agent, illustrated with pictograms (e.g. a patient wearing an EEG cap, a generator or machine), not boxes only.

structure.label: Problem setup
structure.text: 1–4 paragraphs: input and output spaces, labels and the formal goal, in the problem statement's own names.

structure.label: Slot 2 — The borrowed machinery
structure.text: One subsection per pillar the introduction names, in its order: notation first, one paragraph per equation with its where clause, closing on the gap of the piece the proposal modifies.

structure.label: Slot 3 — The proposal
structure.text: Always last: the method as a delta on the machinery, its notation, each contribution defined under the property it delivers, the general combination, and a closing pointer to the summary diagram.

rules: No motivation, result, measured number, comparison or evaluation protocol: training, metrics, baselines, splits and statistics belong to the experimental set-up.
Each mathematical subsection opens on notation, never on an equation; every displayed equation is numbered and cited as Equation (n).
Citations attach to the borrowed object they credit, before its equation; no equation of the proposal carries a citation.
The summary diagram's panels are the contribution list, same count, order and names; no dataset or baseline appears in it.
Every artefact is referenced in the body before it appears.

sections.name: Experimental set-up
sections.extent: 800–3500 words · optional preamble and two subsections · one closing diagram

structure.label: Preamble (optional)
structure.text: One paragraph of 30–80 words, no citations: the purpose of the protocol and the blocks in order.

structure.label: Subsection 1 — Assessment and method comparison
structure.text: The datasets (when methods does not own them; when a real dataset is described, its explanation closes with an acquisition-protocol diagram drawn by the diagram-author agent, illustrated with pictograms, not boxes only), the comparison axes, the competing methods each formalized and cited, the metrics each defined by a numbered equation, qualitative instruments, the statistical test and its unit, and the ablation and sensitivity design.

structure.label: Subsection 2 — Training details
structure.text: Past tense: preprocessing and exclusions, the partition protocol, optimizer and schedule, hyperparameter search with its seed, leakage control, software and hardware.

structure.label: Closing diagram
structure.text: The handoff to the results: data, compared methods, axes, metric per crossing, qualitative instruments and the repetition unit; no internal component of the proposal.

rules: The whole evaluation is declared here and nowhere else; no result is reported.

Comparison criteria, preprocessing, partitions and hypothesis tests are each backed by a citation to work that uses or justifies that protocol (methodological papers or reference books in AI, statistics, health, etc.).
One citation per compared method, swept architecture, qualitative instrument and non-standard metric; standard metrics carry an equation instead.
Paragraphs open on a sentence, never on a bold label or run-in heading; every hyperparameter is a symbol declared in the methods section.
Tables use booktabs inside the text width, with text at 0.70–0.90 of the body size, never scaled below 0.85, caption above.

sections.name: Results and discussion
sections.extent: 1170–4150 words · 2 to 5 content blocks · 3–12 figures and 0–8 tables

structure.label: Block 0 — Controlled scenario
structure.text: When declared: the proposal on data with known ground truth.

structure.label: Block 1 — The general task
structure.text: 40% to 66% of the section: main metric, main data, baselines, closing on the declared statistical test.

structure.label: Block 2 — One block per contribution
structure.text: Each validates its property with the instrument the set-up named; an interpretability contribution is read twice, qualitatively and by its faithfulness measure.

structure.label: Block 3 — Ablation and sensitivity
structure.text: One reading per ablation variant, then each sweep.

structure.label: Block 4 — Cost
structure.text: When cost is claimed: one or two paragraphs and one figure.

structure.label: Block 5 — Limitations
structure.text: Last, always, under its own contract.

rules: Nothing is introduced here: every scenario, metric, baseline, test and ablation was declared in the experimental set-up.
Per artefact, three beats in one paragraph: point at it, read it in numbers, give the mechanism; the pointer resolves to the exact panel, column or row.
The discussion is inferential by default (about 57%), assertive by exception (about 30%), corroborative otherwise (about 13%); no claim without an artefact, no implications for practice.

Interpretive explanations, analyses of a baseline method, and qualitative-interpretability arguments are backed by citations that support the idea; a citation never stands for the paper's own numbers.
No preamble, no closing artefact and no numbered equation; every artefact is referenced before it appears.

sections.name: Limitations
sections.extent: 180–410 words · 1 paragraph, or 2 with a failure mode · 3 to 5 items

structure.label: Opening concession
structure.text: Although / While / Despite a concrete achievement the results support, several limitations must be acknowledged.

structure.label: Each item
structure.text: Name the decision or boundary, concede its benefit, state its cost, state the consequence for the claim, and where possible what the alternative would give and cost.

structure.label: Second paragraph (optional)
structure.text: The quantitative failure mode: the weakest regime, the worst cell of an already reported table, evidence the regime is hard, and the mechanism.

structure.label: Closing (optional)
structure.text: What addressing the limitations would give, or where the field is moving, with a citation.

rules: Every item carries at least one citation, on the alternative that would fix it or on the fact that the problem is known.
Two sweeps: the mathematical section for gaps in the proposal and the experimental design for gaps in the validation.
Every item names a decision in the formulation or in the design, never a feeling.
No figure, table, equation or new measurement.

sections.name: Conclusions

structure.label: Block 1 — The proposal and its components
structure.text: Always first, 60–226 words, past tense: full name, acronym, category, and the components with the same count, order and names as before, closing on what distinguishes the method.

structure.label: Block 2 — The findings
structure.text: One paragraph per contribution, 80–180 words each, at most one headline number per contribution, identical to the results.

structure.label: Block 3 — The consequence beyond the method (optional)
structure.text: About 50–120 words: what an implementer or whoever lives the problem takes away.

structure.label: Block 4 — Future work
structure.text: Always last and its own paragraph, 55–180 words: one direction per relevant limitation, each with one citation.

rules: No equations, figures or tables.
Citations only in the future-work block.
Nothing new: no experiment, comparison or interpretation the results do not already hold.
No future-work direction without a limitation motivating it.

sections.name: Back matter
sections.extent: Declarations after the conclusions and before the references

structure.label: Required blocks
structure.text: Author contributions (37–44 words), funding (about 55 words per project), data availability (7–22 words), code availability (7–25 words), conflicts of interest (one sentence) and the AI-use declaration (40–90 words, always).

structure.label: Conditional blocks
structure.text: Institutional review board and informed consent statements, acknowledgments, supplementary materials, abbreviations, appendices (after the references), and highlights and graphical abstract for Elsevier venues.

structure.label: Placement
structure.text: Where each block lands and its title follow the publisher of the selected venue.

rules: Each declaration is a paragraph of its own, never run together with the one before it.
CRediT roles with author initials; an AI tool is never an author.
Funding carries the project's exact registered title, the funder and the grant code copied from the records.
Data and code availability are separate claims, each with a resolving URL and the date it was checked.
The AI-use declaration states what the pipeline's AI-usage record shows, never less and never more.

general.heading: Cross-cutting rules
rules: One voice for the whole paper: first person plural or impersonal, chosen once; procedures that were run go in the passive past.
Sentences average 21–27 words: one claim and its qualifier, never a chain of three clauses.
Every figure, table or panel is referenced in the body before it appears, and the pointer resolves to the exact sub-element.
Each property keeps the same name from the problem statement to the evidence: problem → contribution → property → instrument → evidence.
Every claim needs a source that holds it; citations are resolved against the bibliography, never invented.
Text in figures and tables prints between 0.70 and 0.90 times the body font size.
The canonical manuscript is single-column review mode with blinded authors until the operator verifies it.
